trust_decision.summary: Whether the peer certificate matches the requested server hostname is decided nowhere: urllib3 marks its stdlib SSLContext check_hostname=True before the connector swaps that context for a PyOpenSSLContext that never checks hostnames, so urllib3 skips its own _match_hostname and every connector HTTPS connection accepts any validly-chained certificate for any name.

landing_point.why: A reader of 'improperly verifies TLS hostnames' looks at the connector's TLS wrap wrapper; lines 159-168 show it substituting a PyOpenSSLContext for the caller's stdlib context and then handshaking, with no hostname comparison anywhere before return.

fix_sites.entry_point: urllib3 HTTPS wrap (all connector HTTPS traffic) via the monkeypatched connection_.ssl_wrap_socket
same wrapper: the context-substitution branch that must carry the replaced stdlib context's hardening forward
_build_context_with_partial_chain called from ssl_wrap_socket_with_ocsp when no PyOpenSSLContext is supplied

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The only other TLS entry point, _openssl_connect, says in its own docstring that it builds 'The OpenSSL connection without validating certificates', so a solver can reasonably call it a diagnostic that the hostname-verification advisory was never about.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Intentional unverified connections must keep working: the diagnostic probe sends a request with verify=False (cert_reqs=CERT_NONE) to detect a transparent proxy, so a fix that fails closed on a missing hostname before honouring verify_mode, or that forces CERT_REQUIRED, breaks `snowflake-connector-diagnostic`. Separately, urllib3's documented alternate verification (assert_hostname / assert_fingerprint, which make urllib3 skip its own hostname match) is bypassed by any check keyed only on server_hostname.

O6_input_shapes: server_hostname present as a plain DNS name (the normal case)
server_hostname is None while verification is required (fail closed, CertificateError) versus CERT_NONE where a missing hostname is tolerated
bracketed IPv6 literal such as [::1] (brackets stripped before the IP test)
scoped IPv6 literal with a %zone suffix (suffix dropped)
caller supplies a stdlib ssl.SSLContext (hardening mirrored) versus supplies none (urllib3 default floor TLS 1.2 + OP_NO_COMPRESSION restored)
Windows-style negative int for SSLContext.options (bit-31 mask recovered as unsigned)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: TLS handshake to the deployment host through _openssl_connect, which builds an OpenSSL.SSL.Connection with no certificate, chain or hostname validation and is reachable from the tool CLIs (probe_connection, dump_ocsp_response, dump_ocsp_response_cache)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Its docstring declares it 'The OpenSSL connection without validating certificates' and it is a diagnostic helper, not a connection that carries Snowflake traffic, so verifying there would defeat its purpose.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the fix; callers in src/snowflake/connector/tool/dump_ocsp_response_cache.py:16, src/snowflake/connector/tool/probe_connection.py:9 and src/snowflake/connector/tool/dump_ocsp_response.py:15

O8b_injection_room.sibling: make PyOpenSSLContext.wrap_socket honour self.check_hostname and match the peer certificate against server_hostname, as the stdlib context does
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is the low-level primitive every pyOpenSSL handshake in the connector goes through and the class already carries a check_hostname attribute (line 424) that nothing reads; upstream urllib3 deliberately left the match to its higher layer, so a maintainer hardening this fork would plausibly add it here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a hand-rolled stdlib wrap_socket in the diagnostic flow that loads certifi, sets VERIFY_X509_PARTIAL_CHAIN and connects (with a CONNECT tunnel) to report cert issuer
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already duplicates the connector's TLS setup in a second module; a maintainer could have mirrored the new post-handshake match (or disabled check_hostname to keep inspecting certs through a proxy) in this same block.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second TLS connector helper (binary-backoff retry loop, SNI set, handshake) that never verifies identity
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It sits in the same module as the fixed wrapper and uses a different TLS stack (raw pyOpenSSL instead of the urllib3 wrapper), which is exactly how a fix lands in one place and a copy in another place is missed.

O9_family: CWE-297 improper validation of certificate with host mismatch (TLS server identity verification)

O10_build.toolchain: setuptools via setup.cfg (python_requires >=3.9), pip install -e ., pytest (<7.5.0 pinned in setup.cfg test extras)
O10_build.project_tests: test/unit/test_ssl_partial_chain.py (context injection, OCSP disabled) and test/unit/test_ssl_partial_chain_handshake.py (loopback TLS handshake against a local cert) already exist and run offline; no hostname-verification test exists at the pinned commit (the fix adds test/unit/test_ssl_hostname_verification.py and test/unit/test_ssl_context_hardening.py as new files); test/integ/* needs a Snowflake account.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Set check_hostname = True on the context (or assume urllib3's existing _match_hostname still runs) and stop: PyOpenSSLContext.check_hostname is a plain attribute that wrap_socket never consults, so nothing changes.

out_of_scope_notes: Unrelated Windows-only OverflowError in pyOpenSSL options marshalling is bundled into the same commit and is a platform defect, not a separate security route.
